_comment: GOLDEN CASES FOR THE ORDER-LIFECYCLE MIRROR PAIR. Read shared/README.md.
Two implementations answer 'is this order finished?', in two languages,
The backend uses it to refuse retiring a subscription that live orders
still reference (TODO-20); the web app uses it to decide what belongs in
Comenzi vs Arhiva (TODO-21). If they disagree, one order is simultaneously
finished and not finished, and nothing in either toolchain notices.
This file is the edge the code cannot express. Both test suites read it.
Add a case here when you change the rule -- in BOTH implementations.

cases.name: every task COMPLETED beats a date still in the future
every task COMPLETED, date already past
one task IN_PROGRESS outranks a past date
all tasks NEW with a past anchor is overdue, not done
all tasks NEW with a future anchor falls through to dates
all tasks NEW anchored exactly today is being worked
no tasks at all, visit date strictly past
no tasks, visit dated today is being worked, not done
no tasks, visit still upcoming
no tasks and no date is unknown, which is NOT fulfilled
an unparseable date is treated as absent, not as a verdict
Ridicare pickup strictly past, no tasks
Ridicare pickup dated today is being worked
Amplasare with no start date is unknown
Amplasare not started yet
Amplasare on site with the window still open
Amplasare ending exactly today is still on site
Amplasare whose window has closed
an indefinite Amplasare is never done by dates alone
a started Amplasare with no end date is still active
task evidence can finish even an indefinite Amplasare

_backendOnlyComment: CANCELLED exists in the backend TaskStatus enum and NOT in the web
TaskStatus union, so these cases cannot be constructed on the web side at
all -- the type forbids it. The web summarizer collapses anything that is
neither COMPLETED nor IN_PROGRESS to NEW, so the OUTCOME is identical;
these exist to pin that equivalence on the side that can express it.
cross_project_invariants.py is what enforces that CANCELLED stays the
only difference between the two status sets.

backendOnlyCases.name: a CANCELLED task behaves exactly like NEW: past anchor is overdue
a CANCELLED task behaves exactly like NEW: future anchor falls through to dates
CANCELLED alongside COMPLETED is not 'all completed'
